title: Tenant-priority burst-curtailment scaling policy
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Dedicated pools must serve multiple tenants with divergent traffic profiles while meeting per-tenant throughput guarantees for committed customers. The existing autoscaler targets global throughput or single aggregated p95 latency, which allows noisy tenants to cause capacity thrash or disproportionate allocations. This ticket designs and implements a tenant-priority, weighted-target autoscaling policy with burst-curtailment so we maintain committed guarantees while bounding cost and preserving stability.

Proposed solution summary:
- Per-tenant SLO targets: each tenant has a primary target metric (e.g., committed throughput, p99 latency, or request success rate) and a tier weight (gold/silver/bronze => weight numeric).
- Weighted target composition: compute a single scalar target for the pool as a weight-sum of per-tenant deficits normalized by their commitments.
- Burst token-bucket curtailment: allow short bursts using tenant-specific token buckets derived from historical burst profiles, with explicit curtail thresholds that trigger temporary rate-limiting and surge-credit accounting instead of immediate scale-ups.
- Staged scaling algorithm: controller with proportional+integral terms (PI) operating on the weighted deficit, with staged step-ups (fast ramp for deficit > 2x target, conservative increments otherwise) and capped step-downs to avoid oscillation.
- Safety envelopes: per-pod max concurrency, global headroom floor (e.g., 15-25%), cooldown windows, surge budget reserve for high-tier tenants, and automatic rollback triggers on error-rate spikes.
- Integration points: routing fallback to lower-cost model variants if scaling can't meet peaks, dashboarding for per-tenant credit usage, and policy knobs surfaced in Console for admins to tune weights and burst budgets.

Why different from prior work: previous tickets optimized autoscaling on throughput or quantile-latency with global heuristics. This design explicitly reasons about multi-tenant fairness and committed guarantees, introducing a creditable burst system to trade short-term elasticity for stability and cost predictability.
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes weighted pool target and exposes metric 'autoscale.weighted_deficit'
Burst token-bucket implemented per-tenant; dashboard shows tokens/usage and curtail events
Staged step-up/down behavior in autoscaler; no >3 full-pod scale-ups within 60s under synthetic surge tests
Safety limits: per-pod concurrency cap applied; global headroom respects configured floor (default 20%)
End-to-end tests: two synthetic tenants (gold with commit, bronze bursty) demonstrate gold tenant maintains committed throughput during bronze burst while autoscaler limits cost
Canary rollout executed to 3 dedicated pools; rollback path verified on induced error spike
Documentation: Console knobs and API docs updated; runbook for troubleshooting curtailment and surge credits

comments: 2025-09-22 Asha Kapoor: Created ticket after customer escalation where a gold tenant's committed throughput dropped during another tenant's sustained burst. Initial design sketch attached.
2025-09-24 Miguel Torres: Prototype token-bucket implemented in simulation harness. Early results show 40-60% fewer scale events for modeled traces. Will open branch 'eng/tenant-burst' by EOD.

2025-09-26 Evelyn Chan: Added PI controller draft. Need to choose per-tenant integral window to avoid credit bleed; proposing 5-min I-term for gold tenants, 1-min for bronze. Feedback requested from SRE.
2025-09-29 Lars Becker: Completed chaos tests for rollback triggers. Induced 8% error spike when we disabled per-pod concurrency cap — confirms cap is necessary. Added test cases to harness.
2025-10-01 Miguel Torres: Opened PR #8421 with core controller and token-bucket plumbing. Requesting review from Asha and Evelyn. Plan to run canary on three pools next week.
2025-10-01 Priya Shah: Console mockups uploaded and feedback provided: show 'burst credits remaining' prominently and a historical chart of curtail events to help customer conversations.
notes: Tradeoffs: Allowing bursts reduces short-term customer impact but makes capacity accounting harder — we're introducing explicit surge-credit debits to keep accounting auditable.
Fallbacks: If pool headroom cannot be created fast enough, routing will fallback to compatible model variants and log a customer-impact event for billing reconciliations.
Operational: Oncall should watch 'curtail.events' and 'credit_depletion' alerts; runbook outlines steps to increase headroom or temporarily adjust weights.
